literal: To those capable of the intimate friendship of not hearing a friend's fault, if friends commit faults daily, [it is acceptable].
translation: For those who possess the capability of intimate friendship that ignores a friend's faults, it is acceptable even if their friends commit lapses every single day.
modern: நண்பர்களின் குற்றங்களைக் கேளாதவாறு கடந்துபோகும் நெருக்கமான நட்புரிமை கொண்டவர்களுக்கு, நண்பர்கள் நாள்தோறும் தவறுகளைச் செய்தாலும் அது குற்றமாகாது.
explanation: This couplet highlights the depth of true, long-standing friendship. The poet explains that those who have the rare capacity to overlook or ignore the faults of their close friends will not find it a problem even if those friends commit lapses every day. The word 'keḻutakaimai' refers to the right of intimacy where one does not take offense at a friend's actions. By 'kēḷā' (not hearing), the poet suggests deliberately ignoring or not paying attention to the shortcomings of loved ones to preserve the bond.
